THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.212/2009 dated 22.07.2011 on the file of the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Mysore.

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.7,55,000/- and the court below had granted compensation globally of an amount of NC: 2023:KHC:37550 Rs.30,000/-.
It is the case of the claimant that on 17.03.2009, he had been to Dinakadamma Temple along with his wife on his motor cycle.

At about 1.15 p.m when they were proceeding near the land of Gopal,
Bannamgadi village, Pandavapura Taluk, a lorry came from Bannamgadi village in a rash and negligent manner and while overtaking the claimant's vehicle dashed to the claimant motor cycle.
As a result, the claimant and his wife fell down and they sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to K.R. Hospital, Mysore and he was admitted as inpatient for one week,
thereafter he had taken treatment at Adithya Hospital and spent huge amount for treatment.
The court below observing that as per Ex.P-7 wound certificate, he had sustained 6 injuries.

Injury No.
1,3,4 and 5 are simple in nature and injury No. 2 and 6 are grievous in nature and granted the global compensation of an amount of Rs.30,000/-.
Learned counsel for the claimant submits that he had sustained six injuries.
Out of that four injuries are simple in nature and two injuries are grievous in nature.
The court below without considering all other aspects had only granted compensation of an amount of Rs.30,000/- globally.
Learned counsel submits that photographs were filed as Ex.P-11 and Ex.P-12.
Learned counsel had drawn the attention of this court to the exhibits and submits that there is disfigurement.
It is submitted that the court below had failed to consider all these aspects and granted meagre amount of Rs.30,000/-.
Hence the claimant is entitled for reasonable compensation and the said compensation needs to be enhanced.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the except marking the documents i.e.,
Ex.P- 1 to Ex.P-12 and examining himself as PW-1, the claimant had not examined the doctor and Raju S/O Late Venkatesh vs Divisional Manager on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199707538/
2 the Tribunal had rightly granted the compensation of Rs.30,000/-.

He submits that NC:
2023:KHC:37550 claimant had failed to make out any grounds for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the entire material on record.
This court had perused the wound certificate Ex.P-7.
As per Ex.P-7 he had sustained 6 injuries.
The wound certificate disclosed that injuries No. 1, 3, 4 and 5 are simple in nature and 2 and 6 are grievous in nature.
Coupled with Ex.P-7, this court has also seen Ex.P-11 and Ex.P-12, the photographs shows that there is disfigurement.
Considering two grievous injuries and four simple injuries he sustained, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
Having sustained six injuries, two grievous, it would take at least two months for him to recover and to resume his work.
According to the claimant, he is a mason and he is earning an amount of Rs.8,000/- per month.

As this accident has taken place in the year 2009, considering the income at Rs.4,500/-, for two months, this court in NC: 2023:KHC:37550 inclined to grant an amount of Rs.9,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
Towards disfigurement an amount of Rs.21,000/- and under the head of Transport, Attendant and extra nourishment another amount of Rs.10,000/- is granted.

6. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER 1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
